title: Cause-conditioned recovery versus the fixed recovery ladder
paper_track: Beyond the Parser / cause-conditioned recovery follow-on
research_question: At an equal per-case recovery budget, does explicitly separating operational/transient failures from semantic/model failures and restricting same-family retry for semantic failures improve trusted-output yield or cost per trusted output relative to the existing cost-ordered fixed ladder?
non_claims: Unit tests are implementation evidence, not empirical proof that cause-conditioned recovery improves quality.
Historical aggregate EXP-0001/EXP-0002/EXP-0004 metrics do not identify counterfactual outcomes for unexecuted recovery operators.
Phase 0 policy-divergence analysis cannot support a quality, latency, or cost-performance claim.
No public, patent-performance, or paper-performance claim is authorized until Phase 1 produces frozen paired evidence and independent review.

implementation_under_test.required_runtime_identity: immutable qualified runtime; exact image/model/evaluator revisions frozen before Phase 1

failure_classes.SEMANTIC_MODEL: source-preserving deterministic repair may run, but same-family parser/model variation is ineligible; next eligible operator must be independent-family, source verifier, reconciliation, review, or fail-closed
failure_classes.STATE_INTEGRITY: not guessed transient; existing fail-closed/reconciliation policy remains authoritative

phase_0.name: policy-divergence feasibility
phase_0.input_contract: per-case rows containing case_id, failure_code, failure_signature, and observed recovery history; aggregate metrics are rejected
outputs: estimated GPU/cost-unit difference from selected policy metadata
go_to_phase_1_if: a non-trivial set of public-corpus cases has policy divergence
the divergent cases can be reconstructed from immutable source/primary-output artifacts
both recovery arms are executable under the same frozen runtime/evaluator contract

phase_1.name: paired intervention on policy-divergent cases
phase_1.data: public-source documents only; no customer documents
phase_1.case_selection: freeze the eligible case manifest before executing either recovery arm; stratify semantic/model failures by failure code and document family, with an operational/transient control stratum
held_constant: primary parser/model output presented to recovery
execution_economy: if fixed and cause-conditioned selectors choose the same action, execute it once and share the measured result between arms
only policy-divergent cases require two recovery executions
ground truth/evaluator labels never mount on GPU workers; GPU receives source-only inputs and outputs are scored locally
phase_1.primary_endpoint: trusted-output rate among policy-divergent semantic/model cases
secondary_endpoints: incremental recovery yield by FailureClass and FailureCode
catastrophic or newly introduced critical failure count
phase_1.trusted_output_definition: the recovery output passes the frozen source-grounded acceptance contract and applicable official/local integrity evaluator without a newly introduced critical failure; parser/model self-confidence or candidate agreement alone can never make an output trusted
statistics: report numerator and denominator for every rate
bootstrap confidence interval for paired yield/cost deltas where sample size permits
break out results by failure class/code and document family

stop_before_spend_if: formal immutable runtime is not READY/qualified
required source-only artifacts are missing or hash-mismatched
predicted pilot spend exceeds nominal cap without a smaller informative cohort
provider/runtime identity cannot be held constant across arms
pilot.hard_cap_rule: never exceed USD 10 without a new explicit founder authorization

claim_gate.phase_1_failure: retain null/negative result; do not tune the registered endpoint after observing outcomes
claim_gate.phase_1_success: may support a narrowly scoped empirical statement only with corpus, denominator, runtime/evaluator revisions, confidence interval, and receipt hashes; external publication remains separately blocked by IP-2/publication controls
